problem: The point $B$ has spherical coordinates $(2\sqrt{3},\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{6}).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $B.$
worked_solution:
If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Calculating $x$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot 0\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating $y$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot 1\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculating $z$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $B$ are $(0,\sqrt{3},3).$
